What Is Really Behind Nike Stock's Run?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Nike (NKE) is deliberately reducing some of its own sales by supplying fewer of its lifestyle shoes, and that strategy may be what Nike bulls are counting on. You probably read falling sales as a sign that shoppers are leaving Nike, but part of that decline is planned. Nike stock returned 17.0% from October 6 to November 4, 2026, though it is still down 31.7% over the past year. Part of the rise came on October 15, when Nike gained 5.2% as buyers moved into beaten-down consumer stocks and away from the AI trade. So how much of Nike's sales fall is its own choice?

Nike reduced revenue from the Dunk, part of its NIKE Sportswear business, by nearly 50% in fiscal Q1 2027 as planned. Management said this cut cost Sportswear roughly $200 million in revenue, compared to a $507 million drop in Nike's total revenue from a year earlier. That single planned reduction accounts for a large part of the quarter's drop.

The Dunk is not the only product facing reductions. Revenue for the Jordan Brand, which made up 13% of Nike's business in the quarter, fell by a mid-teens percentage, a figure management provided to demonstrate the scale of its quarterly cuts. The company also plans to reduce the volume and frequency of specific Jordan Retro launches. In Greater China, where revenue fell 26%, Nike is eliminating distribution through channels that do not fit its strategy.

Not all of the decline was intentional, however. Management said some older, high-volume Sportswear shoes sold below expectations, and noted that shoppers are cautious. So a large part of the quarter's fall is planned, with weak demand on top.

Management says the cuts will mean less deep discounting of Nike's brands and stronger full-price sales. Nike has not shown that payoff yet. Its quarterly gross margin was 42.8% in fiscal Q1 2027, up from 42.2% in fiscal Q1 2026, but management credited supply chain cost management and currency gains, which were partly offset by more discounting.
Meanwhile, Nike is not finished shrinking. Management expects fiscal 2027 revenue to decline in the high single digits, and expects EBIT, its operating profit, to fall by a greater percentage.

sum: As the 2026 investing year winds down, more investors are analyzing their portfolios and preparing for 2027. For some investors, it may mean cutting positions or making sure they aren't overly concentrated in one specific area.

Others may be worried they have too many growth stocks and not enough income stocks. With Nike's (NYSE: NKE) dividend yielding a respectable 4.2%, it may seem like a good addition to a portfolio. However, a closer look reveals more considerations are needed than just yield.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

When CEO Elliott Hill, a longtime Nike veteran who joined the company in the late 1980s as a sales representative intern, took over in 2024, he had his work cut out for him. Nike had made a series of missteps over the years, ranging from shunning wholesalers to failing to keep up with changes in consumer tastes.

A finalized turnaround under Hill, however, hasn't quite happened. For its fiscal 2027 first-quarter earnings, Nike reported revenue of $11.2 billion, down 4% from the prior-year period. Along with that drop in overall revenue, Nike also saw its net income decrease 2% to $712 million.

Adding more woes to the rough quarter, Nike announced a restructuring plan expected to lead to layoffs and forecast that 2027 full-year revenue will fall by a high-single-digit percentage. With the stock price down around 39% so far in 2026, there don't appear to be any immediate catalysts to reverse those losses. With that gloomy full-year 2027 sales forecast, Nike doesn't seem likely to beat analyst estimates or be in a position to boost its outlook anytime soon.

That said, as much as Nike's sales have been an issue, there's also a brewing issue of expectations that could continue to weigh on the stock. There's a perception problem with Nike, and the market still hasn't quite caught on that the iconic retailer may need to be reevaluated.

NIKE vs. adidas: Which Stock Offers Stronger Growth Potential?
sum: The global sportswear industry is witnessing an intensifying battle for market dominance as industry heavyweights NIKE, Inc. NKE and adidas AG ADDYY compete for consumer loyalty, innovation leadership and market share. NIKE remains the world's leading athletic footwear and apparel company, while Germany-based adidas stands as its formidable challenger, leveraging its sporting heritage, product innovation and strong lifestyle appeal.

Both companies design, market and distribute athletic footwear, apparel and accessories through wholesale networks, company-operated stores and digital platforms. While NIKE is focused on revitalizing its brand momentum and defending its market leadership, adidas is capitalizing on evolving consumer preferences and lifestyle trends. Against this backdrop, which sportswear giant offers stronger investment potential? Let us find out.

NIKE maintains a dominant position in the global sporting goods industry, supported by a diversified portfolio of footwear, apparel and accessories. Its Performance business generated $16 billion in fiscal 2026 revenues and grew in the high single digits in first-quarter fiscal 2027. Running delivered double-digit growth, while NIKE nearly tripled its share of the Max cushioning category in the past year, reinforcing its competitive strength.

NIKE's Sport Offense strategy emphasizes innovation, sport-specific assortments and stronger consumer engagement. Its portfolio spans Running, Basketball, Football, Training and Sportswear, targeting athletes and lifestyle-conscious consumers. Women's Basketball signature revenues expanded nearly 500% between fiscal 2022 and 2026. Meanwhile, NIKE is strengthening digital distribution in China, restoring Jordan Brand exclusivity and leveraging product innovations to reinforce its premium positioning.

However, financial headwinds persist. First-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues declined 4% to $11.2 billion, reflecting weakness in Sportswear, Jordan Brand and Greater China. Nevertheless, the gross margin improved 60 basis points to 42.8%, while earnings reached 48 cents per share. Its Pace transformation initiative targets $2.5 billion in savings, potentially supporting operational efficiency and long-term profitability despite near-term revenue pressures.

Nike shares tumble after weak revenue outlook and layoff plans underway
sum: Nike shares dropped Friday, falling for a second straight day after the company reported declining revenue and plans to lay off staff in 2027.

The sportswear giant said Thursday that its fiscal first-quarter revenues were down 4% to $11.2 billion, citing declines in Greater China, which was partially offset by growth in its North America segment. Its net income was $712 million, down 2% from $727 million the previous year.

"We have more work to do in NIKE Sportswear, Jordan Brand and Greater China, and we're taking deliberate actions to strengthen those businesses the right way for the long term," Nike President and CEO Elliott Hill said in the release.
Nike expects revenues to decline in the high-single digits in 2027. Its shares were last down about 6% in morning trading on Friday and have declined nearly 45% since the beginning of the year.
The company also announced its new operating model "Pace," which is expected to deliver $2.5 billion in cost savings by 2031, with plans to lay off more staff starting in 2027.

"This work will result in fewer roles across Nike, and I want to acknowledge that news like this creates uncertainty. I don't take that lightly," Hill said in a separate announcement on Thursday. "Decisions about impacted roles related to this work will begin in calendar year 2027 and beyond."

The program also includes efforts to modernize Nike's global supply chain, organizing into three geographies, establishing a new campus in India, and further streamlining the organization to reduce costs.

sum: The global athletic footwear and apparel market has long been defined by one of the fiercest rivalries in consumer goods — NIKE Inc. NKE versus adidas AG ADDYY. Together, the two sportswear powerhouses command the industry's largest global market shares, leveraging iconic brands, innovation-driven product portfolios, and expansive retail and digital ecosystems to stay ahead of the competition. Nike continues to hold the top position in athletic footwear and apparel worldwide, while adidas has strengthened its standing with renewed momentum across performance sports and lifestyle categories, particularly in footwear.

Although both companies operate in the same core businesses of athletic footwear, apparel and accessories, their paths to leadership differ. NIKE has built its dominance through unmatched scale, athlete endorsements, direct-to-consumer expansion and continuous product innovation. Meanwhile, adidas has blended performance credibility with cultural relevance, capitalizing on strong franchises in football, running and Originals to expand its global footprint.

As consumer preferences evolve and competition intensifies, the battle between these two industry leaders is increasingly about protecting market share while capturing the next wave of growth. In this face-off, we compare NIKE and adidas to determine which sportswear giant offers the stronger competitive position for investors today.

NIKE remains the world's largest athletic footwear and apparel company, commanding an estimated share of more than 40% of the global athletic footwear market and maintaining unmatched brand equity across performance sports. Its powerful brand equity is supported by a portfolio spanning Nike, Jordan and Converse, and leadership across running, basketball, football and lifestyle categories. Still, its turnaround faces strain. Sportswear and Jordan Streetwear, together representing roughly half of revenues, remain weak amid softer traffic, discounting and pressured discretionary spending.
Management acknowledged that macroeconomic pressures and sluggish traffic have delayed the top-line recovery, even as performance categories continue to outperform.

sum: Nike, Inc. (ISIN US6541061031) stock is trading near a 12-year low around USD 38.40 as of September 4, 2026, after losing roughly 78 percent from its November 2021 peak near USD 179 per share, according to recent market overviews.Fortune India For long-term investors, the combination of index demotion and weaker fundamentals has turned Nike into a turnaround story rather than a growth stalwart.

The most immediate catalyst for Nike stock is its removal from the S&P 100 index later in September 2026, following an announcement by S&P Dow Jones Indices that the change will take effect before trading opens on September 21, 2026.INDmoney This ends nearly 18 years of Nike’s membership in the large-cap benchmark, although the company will remain in the S&P 500 and continue to trade on the New York Stock Exchange.GuruFocus Index exits of this kind often force passive funds tracking the benchmark to sell, adding mechanical pressure around the effective date.

Market data show that Nike shares closed at USD 38.40 on September 4, 2026, down 0.95 percent from the prior session and roughly 50 percent below a cited 52-week high of USD 76.97, marking their lowest level in about 12 years.Fortune India At that close, the company’s equity value stood near USD 57 billion, compared with roughly USD 280 billion at the November 2021 peak, implying a market-capitalization decline of about USD 224 billion over less than five years.INDmoney For investors, that kind of drawdown is a clear sign that both earnings power and the valuation multiple have reset.

The steep share-price decline has come alongside a meaningful drop in Nike’s earnings per share and pressure on key markets such as China. According to one recent analysis, Nike’s share price has fallen 78.6 percent from USD 179.10 on November 5, 2021 to USD 38.40 on September 4, 2026, while underlying EPS is down 55.6 percent versus fiscal 2021 and the price-to-earnings multiple has compressed from about 50 times to around 24 times earnings.INDmoney That quantified linkage between earnings and valuation helps explain why the stock is not just cheaper but also priced for slower growth.

sum: (Corrects to remove reference to forecast of surprise drop in annual revenue in headline and paragraph 1, removes reference to analysts estimates in paragraph 7; corrects forecast period to fiscal 2027 first half, from full year, in headline, paragraphs 1 and 7)
June 30 (Reuters) – Nike forecast a drop in fiscal 2027 first-half revenue, as the sportswear giant’s turnaround struggles to find its footing, in the face of competition and elevated inventory.

The outlook disappointed investors who have grown impatient with CEO Elliott Hill’s nearly two-year turnaround effort to revamp the business by clearing out excess inventory and reviving product innovation.
Nike’s shares have fallen 35% so far this year and were down about 4% in extended trading on Tuesday despite the company beating estimates for quarterly results.

Hill, who took the helm of the company in 2024, vowed to refocus Nike on key sports like soccer and running. He has also aimed to rebuild relationships with wholesale retailers, many of which had been severed as part of former CEO John Donahoe’s pivot to a direct-to-consumer model.
Hill reiterated on a post-earnings call that progress in the company’s efforts to improve its sports-focused product line “continue to be uneven.”
The company would introduce more than a dozen new footwear styles in its sportswear collection, but the work would take time to scale and translate into consistent results, Hill added.
